package_info.why_malicious: This article does not describe a specific malicious package or code, but rather discusses the limitations of traditional application security testing (AST) tools (SAST, DAST, SCA) in detecting modern software supply chain threats such as malware, code tampering, and backdoors in third-party and open-source software.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code execution in third-party or open-source dependencies
Code tampering in digitally signed or trusted software
Malicious code introduced via typosquatting or lookalike package names
Bypassing commit controls or introducing functional vulnerabilities
file_indicators: Files with names or versions similar to popular packages (typosquatting)
Unexpected modifications in build scripts or update channels
Presence of unauthorized binaries or scripts in third-party packages
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments
Connections to domains not associated with the legitimate software vendor
Exfiltration of secrets or sensitive data to unknown endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: To detect modern software supply chain threats, supplement traditional SAST, DAST, and SCA with behavioral analysis of third-party and open-source packages. Monitor for code tampering, unexpected network activity, and unauthorized file modifications in build and deployment pipelines. Use threat intelligence to identify typosquatting and lookalike packages, and validate the integrity of all software components, including those from trusted vendors.
